Only observation normalization can change the visited-state distribution; action choices cannot.
Each gradient update improves the current loss, so future collected experience must have the same quality.
The new decisions alter which situations are visited, so the learning data distribution can change.

stem: A hypothetical navigation reward pays +1 every time the robot enters a marked cell, without requiring progress to the goal. It learns to loop through the cell. Which diagnosis best matches the lecture’s warning?

options.text: The problem proves that every dense reward is invalid.
The looping behavior proves that the positive shaping reward and the goal objective are equivalent.
The specified reward can be maximized without achieving the intended navigation objective.
The robot failed to maximize the reward because it repeatedly earns it.

assumptions: Added hypothetical loop scenario, not reported case-study behavior.

citations.locator: Lecture 38, physical PDF page 1194, printed footer 30: Reward Design warning about unintended ways to maximize reward.

stem: If a complex maze supplies positive reward only at a rarely reached goal, what training difficulty is highlighted?

options.text: The Q network can no longer produce values for non-goal observations.
Exploration may rarely discover informative successful outcomes.
Sparse rewards make an exploration policy unnecessary because non-goal states have no learning significance.
The absence of immediate reward means future reward cannot influence any predecessor value.

stem: A neural controller learns both a policy that selects actions and a critic that estimates expected return. Which interpretation matches the combined family?

options.text: The actor predicts the next image, while the critic always returns wheel torque.
The critic is necessarily a copy of the actor with identical output meanings.
Having two learned networks makes the system model-based even without a dynamics predictor.
It learns decision and evaluation functions; a transition model is not implied merely by having both.
